chapter: The district underworld and street musicians
title: Walter Preston's band at Tom Anderson's, and the guitarist Snow
summary: Walter Preston, Tom Brown, Charlie Washington and Snow played mandolin and guitars at Tom Anderson's and the halfway house; Dawson sometimes played bass, and the talk wanders into nose candy.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You don't remember his name? Did you know Walter Preston?
Walter Preston, yeah, I know Walter.
Who did he play with?

Well, he, he played with that, it wasn't such a big band, it was just about three or four pieces, or five pieces, I think it was Walter Preston, Tom Brown, uh, Charlie Washington, and, uh, let's see, what's that guy named, uh, I can't think of the bass player. But anyway, sometimes I used to play bass with them, too. And they used to go out, they used to play out at the halfway house, though. They had a, a place on that side of the halfway house, you could go in and play music. And then from there they'd go out to the, to the West End.
Was Charlie Washington any kind of Lonzo Washington?
I don't know, I wouldn't know.
You wouldn't know, you knew both those guys, though.

Yeah, I know both of them, yeah. But he was a guitar player, and he'd sing and entertain, you know. Charlie. Yeah, yeah. And, uh, uh, Anderson, Tom Anderson, uh, is the biggest place I know the way they played at. Mm-hmm. Uh, uh, Walter Preston, and Tom Brown on a mandolin, well, he played mandolin like I was playing, and, uh, uh, Charlie Washington on a guitar, too. They had another fella played guitar called Snow. His nickname was Snow, but I never did know his first name. We used to call him Snow. They had two guitars. Mandolin, two guitars, and a bass.
And that's all you ever knew?
That's all, yeah. But they played at Tom Anderson. I worked there with them.
First try. April the 5th, 1972. Okay.
What were we talking about, Snow? Snow, guitar player, yeah. Why did he call him Snow? That's a nickname.
Why did he call him Snow? What did he...
Don't know if I know.
Was he Snow White?
No, as black as he could be.
Did he sniff Snow?
I don't know what caused him, but they called him Snow. That was a nickname. Now they never did know his right name.
Did they have much nose candy then? Did you ever hear of nose candy?
No, no.
You know, they used to take those ignorant kids and tell them they were sniffing nose candy. And they would be giving them cocaine and stuff like that. Did you ever hear of that?
No, I didn't. I know they had cocaine, but they used to sniff snuff and everything. Yeah.
